executive_summary.headline: What changed
executive_summary.body: Monday’s digest skews agent security: three fresh papers — long-context prompt injection, quantization-triggered backdoors, and out-of-band policy enforcement at a trusted tool boundary — plus DHH’s Omarchy shipping its default user with a root escalation path, a concrete reminder that agent privilege is a host-level problem, not just a prompt problem. The tooling side delivered too: OpenClaw 2.0 is the platform’s largest release yet, and Simon Willison published the most complete hands-on map of ChatGPT Work so far — useful before you spend on a $20/mo sub. Five arXiv papers and a sources-say shift toward outcome-based agent pricing round it out. ## Agent frameworks & tooling - **OpenClaw 2

executive_summary.headline: Why it matters
executive_summary.body: The strongest signals point toward governed, measurable AI workflows rather than isolated model demos.
